nodes.label: SmartStore planning and specification session
nodes.rationale: Contains the product plan, PRD, feature requirements, roadmap, relational schema, REST API specification, UAT cases, and NestJS folder structure generated for SmartStore.

nodes.label: SmartStore POS and Inventory
nodes.rationale: The product is a single-store smartphone-shop system combining inventory control and cashier POS operations.

nodes.label: Single-store smartphone retail constraint
nodes.rationale: The MVP targets one physical smartphone store and explicitly excludes multi-store or branch transfer scope.

nodes.label: IDR English web application
nodes.rationale: The selected market configuration is English UI, Indonesian Rupiah currency, and a web application for smartphone retail.

nodes.label: Eight-week MVP delivery target
nodes.rationale: The plan sets an eight-week MVP with foundation, inventory, POS, reporting, UAT, and launch milestones.

nodes.label: IMEI-level inventory traceability
nodes.rationale: A core objective is complete traceability for serialized smartphones across receipt, sale, return, and status history.

nodes.label: SmartStore business success KPIs
nodes.rationale: Success is measured by inventory accuracy, checkout speed, daily sales closure, return processing time, and gross-margin visibility.

nodes.label: Procurement to stock workflow
nodes.rationale: The primary inventory flow is create purchase order, receive goods, and update stock.

nodes.label: POS checkout workflow
nodes.rationale: The sale flow adds an item, applies discount and tax, accepts payment, and produces a receipt.

nodes.label: Return and refund workflow
nodes.rationale: The return flow validates the original receipt and IMEI, refunds or credits the customer, and synchronizes stock.

nodes.label: End-of-day reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Day close summarizes sales, payments, returns, and discrepancies for owner review.

nodes.label: Product catalog and supplier master data
nodes.rationale: Master data covers SKU, product name, category, brand, cost/selling prices, tax class, product type, and supplier records.

nodes.label: IMEI registry and status lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Each serialized phone unit has a globally unique IMEI and controlled statuses such as in_stock, sold, returned, and defective.

nodes.label: Purchase orders and goods receiving
nodes.rationale: Purchase orders have a status lifecycle, while receiving records quantities and exact IMEI lists for serialized lines.

nodes.label: Inventory adjustments, cycle counts, and low-stock alerts
nodes.norm_label: inventory adjustments cycle counts low stock alerts
nodes.rationale: Inventory requirements include reason-coded adjustments, approval for large variances, physical cycle counts, and per-SKU low-stock thresholds.

nodes.label: POS pricing, tax, payment, and receipt controls
nodes.norm_label: pos pricing tax payment receipt controls
nodes.rationale: POS supports item/cart discounts, role limits, inclusive or exclusive tax, IDR rounding, cash/transfer/e-wallet/mixed payment, change, and controlled receipt reprints.

nodes.label: Return validation and restock policy
nodes.rationale: Returns must match the original sold item and IMEI, obey a configurable window, and route stock as sellable or defective.

nodes.label: Operational reports and dashboard
nodes.rationale: Reporting covers sales by time/product/staff/payment, gross profit and margin, stock valuation and movement, returns, date filters, and CSV/PDF export.

nodes.label: POS non-functional requirements
nodes.rationale: Requirements specify responsive desktop/tablet usability, fast POS item adds, availability, password/session security, atomic stock updates, no negative stock by default, and daily backups.

nodes.label: MVP scope and release priorities
nodes.rationale: P0 includes authentication, catalog, IMEI, receiving, POS, payments, receipts, returns, reports, and audit; cycle counts, alerts, approvals, and exports are mainly P1.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL relational data model
nodes.rationale: The schema uses relational master, serialized inventory, purchasing, sales, returns, stock accounting, settings, and audit tables linked by foreign keys and indexes.

nodes.label: Atomic stock and IMEI transaction invariants
nodes.rationale: Receiving, sale, return, and adjustment posting must update business records, balances, movements, and serialized status atomically, rolling back on failure.

nodes.label: REST API v1 contract
nodes.rationale: The API specification defines the /api/v1 base, Bearer JWT authentication, JSON responses/errors, resource endpoints, error codes, and permission matrix.

nodes.label: NestJS modular backend architecture
nodes.rationale: The backend structure separates auth, users/roles, catalog, suppliers, IMEI, purchasing, receiving, inventory, sales, returns, reports, settings, audit, and health modules over PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: UAT and go-live acceptance gate
nodes.rationale: UAT requires critical flows, IMEI lifecycle, stock/payment/report accuracy, permissions, reconciliation, no critical defects, and owner sign-off before launch.

nodes.label: Risk-first eight-week implementation roadmap
nodes.norm_label: risk first eight week implementation roadmap
nodes.rationale: The roadmap delivers highest-risk IMEI integrity, stock transactions, and POS finalization early, with weekly release gates and UAT before launch.

nodes.label: Initial scaffold validation findings
nodes.rationale: The generated scaffold initially lacked an ESLint binary and then exposed TypeScript issues around PartialType imports, DTO typing, and JWT expiresIn types.

edges.context: The session goal is a web app for smartphone-store inventory control and cashier POS.
The session defines the eight-week phases and M1-M4 milestones.
The session contains DATABASE_SCHEMA.md and its relational ER overview.
The session contains API_SPEC.md with REST conventions and authentication.
The session contains UAT_TEST_CASES.md and its entry/exit criteria.
The session contains BACKEND_FOLDER_STRUCTURE.md with module responsibilities and transaction boundaries.
The product definition and scope are explicitly single-store smartphone retail.
The selected target market specifies smartphone store, Rupiah, English, and an eight-week web-app MVP.
IMEI traceability is a stated product objective and business problem response.
The product objectives are evaluated through the listed operational KPIs.
The MVP scope includes role-based access and the defined roles have distinct duties.
The PRD separates MVP in-scope functions from out-of-scope multi-store, accounting, CRM, and marketplace features.
The workflow's create-PO and receive-goods steps are specified by purchasing and receiving features.
POS entry searches catalog products by SKU, name, barcode, or IMEI.
The workflow explicitly applies discount/tax and accepts payment before receipt generation.
Completing a serialized sale changes the selected IMEI status to SOLD.
The data-integrity requirements call for atomic stock updates and database-enforced IMEI uniqueness.
Returns are defined around eligibility, refund method, and sellable-versus-defective restocking.
The PRD return flow includes writing an audit log after refund and stock handling.
Day close relies on sales, payment, return, and KPI summaries.
Owner review at close uses the daily KPI dashboard.
Serialized product type determines whether units require the IMEI registry.
Supplier master records feed purchase order creation and receiving.
Unique IMEI records and valid status transitions provide serialized-unit history.
Adjustments must be visible in movement history and approval rules must be enforced before posting.
Low-stock alerts appear on the dashboard/list and can be filtered or exported.
Tax mode, rate, and rounding are configured by store settings.
Discount maximums and high-discount approvals are controlled by role.
Quote, sale, payment, and receipt behaviors are represented by REST endpoints.
Return eligibility uses a configurable policy window.
Revenue, COGS, stock, movement, and return reports aggregate transactional tables.
The API exposes sales, profit, stock, movement, and returns report endpoints with export formats.
Settings changes are listed among actions requiring activity logs.
Atomic stock updates and protection against negative stock are explicit data-integrity requirements.
The schema models stock movements, balances, IMEI links, and transaction references needed for integrity.
The backend architecture assigns QueryRunner/transaction boundaries to receiving, sales, returns, and adjustment services.
The REST contract is implemented by the NestJS controllers/modules described in the backend structure.
The common backend layer includes JWT, roles, and permissions guards.
The roadmap is the implementation form of the eight-week MVP target.
Week 8 requires UAT sign-off, data migration, backup/restore drill, and all MVP acceptance criteria.
UAT explicitly verifies the IMEI lifecycle across receiving, sale, return, and adjustment.
UAT exit requires finance and stock totals to reconcile in the daily close report.
The session records historical typecheck failures, while the later project context records the corrective fixes and passing state.
